summary_brief: 2026年4月19日，AI Agent生态在经历4月中旬"安全系统性加固"和"记忆架构分化"两波高峰后，今日出现值得关注的新方向分化——Anthropic Python/TypeScript SDK同步发布S3/Redis/Postgres SessionStore多后端适配器，标志着SDK生态正从"功能扩展期"转向"生产级统一化"阶段，是4月13日Vercel AI SDK v6发布以来SDK成熟化的最新落地动作。延续趋势方面：安全修复继续跨多个主流Agent框架传播（OpenDevin MCP日志API密钥泄露、OpenClaw WhatsApp认证），跨平台兼容性问题（macOS locale/Intel Mac）同步推进，聊天模块性能优化进入精细化收敛阶段（ClawX RPC超时/重复渲染）。新增推进点：①OpenCode迁移Effect Schema（12281行废弃FastAPI V0清理）代表大型Agent项目进入代码库现代化深水区；②OpenClaw和Deer-Flow同步大规模投资测试基础设施（50+ fixture/Playwright E2E），暗示项目对生产稳定性的要求已超越功能开发本身。整体信号密度41个（高影响7个），高于4月均值但未超越4月16日峰值（45%高影响比 vs 16日51%），生态在高位稳态运行，叙事焦点从"安全修复"和"记忆工程"逐步切换至"SDK统一化+代码质量基础设施"。

engineering_signals.title: AI Agent SDK 生态统一化：SessionStore 多后端支持
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: Anthropic Python/TS SDK 同步发布 S3/Redis/Postgres 存储适配器，配合 Claude Agent SDK TypeScript 的 PR-0 参考实现，标志着 SDK 生态在存储层面向生产环境迈出重要一步，降低了企业级部署的集成门槛。

engineering_signals.title: 安全加固成为多项目共同优先项
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenDevin 修复 WebSocket/MCP 日志中的 API 密钥泄露（评分5），OpenClaw 加固 WhatsApp 认证持久化，OpenDevin PR-3 修复 MCP 配置日志中的 tavilyApiKey 等敏感凭据泄露。安全漏洞跨多个主流 Agent 框架同时被发现和修复，提示供应链安全需加强关注。

engineering_signals.title: 跨平台兼容性统一推进

engineering_signals.title: 聊天模块性能优化与稳定性收敛
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: ClawX 集中修复了 Execution Graph 重构、RPC 超时隐藏、重复渲染请求等多个性能问题（pr-8, pr-11, pr-13），OpenClaw 修复 Cron 去重问题（commit-19），Deer-Flow 修复消息幂等性问题（pr-1）。聊天/对话系统作为核心交互界面的稳定性优化成为工程重点。

engineering_signals.title: 测试基础设施大规模投资
engineering_signals.why_it_matters: OpenClaw 新增 50+ 共享测试 fixture 覆盖 auth/model/cache/sandbox 模块（commit-4），Deer-Flow 引入 Playwright E2E 测试基础设施（commit-7）。两个主流 Agent 框架同步加强测试体系建设，暗示对生产环境稳定性的更高要求。

engineering_signals.title: 代码库现代化：Effect Schema 与遗留代码清理

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing

The only safeguard is a UserWarning at construction time which is silently swallowed in most production configurations (e.g., -W ignore, logging pipelines). An attacker or prompt-injected LLM can execute arbitrary code with full host privileges, leading to credential theft, lateral movement, and data destruction.

signals.topic: DeepResearchAgent KeyError when model returns thinking block before text block (e.g., Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FPB)

The KeyError propagates to tool output, causing the agent to fail silently and return error text instead of the research result. Count=1 is within bounds for P1 when review_reason provides explicit main-flow-blocking evidence. The hard-coded index access pattern is fragile and will likely affect other models with similar thinking-block patterns.

signals.topic: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() omitzero 导致多轮 Agentic Loop 报 400 错误
signals.summary: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() 中 json omitzero 标签在 stdout/stderr/return_code 为零值时静默丢弃字段，导致多轮 Agentic Loop 下一轮 API 调用返回 400 错误（API 将空内容误解析为 error variant schema 并拒绝）
aliases: omitzero silently drops zero-value fields in ToParam()
signals.review_reason: 用户痛点明确：(1) 主流程阻断——多轮 Agentic Loop 在遇到成功执行的 code_execution 返回（最常见场景：ReturnCode=0, empty Stderr/Stdout）时下一轮必败 400；(2) 高可信度生产影响——issue 明确标注'Reliably reproducible in production when code-review agents loop through 20+ tool calls with thinking enabled'；(3) 系统性根因——omitzero 静默丢弃零值字段是结构性缺陷，影响所有 server tool result block 的 ToParam() 方法（已波及 WebSearchToolResultBlock #242、ToolSearchToolResultBlock #317、CodeExecutionToolResultBlock #322 三处）；(4) 非边缘场景——所有使用 code_execution 工具的多轮 agent 场景均受影响，属于 SDK 核心路径。

source_issues.title: CodeExecutionToolResultBlock.ToParam() drops stdout/stderr/return_code via omitzero (same class as #242, #317)
source_issues.evidence: Omitzero tags on CodeExecutionResultBlockParam silently drop zero-value stdout/stderr/return_code fields during re-serialization. When a code execution returns zero/empty values (ReturnCode=0, empty Stderr/Stdout — very common), the content object becomes {"type": "code_execution_result"} only, not matching any valid variant shape, causing 400 from API on next agentic-loop iteration. Reliably reproduced in production when code-review agents loop through 20+ tool calls with thinking enabled. Same pattern as #317 (ToolSearchToolResultBlock) and #242 (WebSearchToolResultBlock). Workaround exists but is not part of the SDK.

signals.topic: Structured Output schema generation ignores Java nullability, causing LLM hallucination and cost waste
signals.summary: The Java SDK's internal schema generator for Structured Output treats all Java class/record fields as required regardless of nullability annotations or Optional types. This forces LLMs to hallucinate values ("null", empty strings, dashes) to satisfy schema constraints, degrading output quality and increasing API costs.
aliases: required array over-inclusion in schema generation
Java reflection schema generator not respecting @Nullable
signals.review_reason: User pain point: Structured Output feature is functionally broken for Java users. Workaround attempts (3 distinct approaches) all fail. Impact is concrete: LLM hallucination of placeholder values, quality degradation of structured output, and increased API token costs. Count=1 limits to P1 despite being a feature-critical issue. The @Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and Optional annotations are all industry-standard nullability markers whose complete ignorance by the schema generator is a clear SDK defect.

source_issues.title: [Java SDK] Structured Output: Java fields are always included in the required array, ignoring nullability markers
source_issues.evidence: User reports that @jakarta.annotation.Nullable, @javax.annotation.Nullable, @JsonProperty(required=false), and java.util.Optional are all ignored by the schema generator. The LLM is forced to hallucinate values (string 'null', empty string, dash) to satisfy required field constraints, even when system prompt says to leave missing fields empty. This directly impacts output quality and causes unnecessary API token consumption.

Apify MCP server incompatible with CMA

signals.topic: beta.files.upload fails with PathLike objects in tuple form — code path unreachable
signals.summary: When passing a PathLike object as the second element of a tuple to beta.files.upload (e.g., file=('foo.txt', Path('foo.txt'), 'text/plain')), the upload fails because the tuple handling code path prevents the PathLike reading code from being reached.
aliases: files.upload PathLike second element tuple unreachable code path

Not a main-flow block but is a clear SDK bug that contradicts documented type hints. Affects file upload functionality in beta API. Low frequency but clear reproduction and root cause.

source_issues.title: [BUG] `client.beta.files.upload` `PathLike` error
source_issues.evidence: Type hints indicate PathLike is supported in tuple form, but _transform_file in _files.py has unreachable code for PathLike handling inside tuples because the tuple case is caught first. Results in a runtime failure.

signals.topic: Bundled CLI version lags behind, silently disabling 1-hour prompt cache TTL for API-key users causing material cost overruns
signals.summary: SDK v0.1.59 bundles CLI 2.1.105 which predates the ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var (added in 2.1.108). API-key users cannot opt into 1-hour cache TTL, causing all cache writes to be billed at the 5-minute tier across hundreds of thousands of agent turns. Production sessions (16-60 min) are most penalized. Anthropic devrel publicly claimed customers get caching savings automatically, which is false for API-key SDK users.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent, production-affecting bug with direct financial impact. The bundled CLI version is hard-pinned to a version that predates a critical feature, and the env var is silently dropped with no warning. The user has explicit cost evidence from session usage files showing 5-minute TTL vs 1-hour TTL. This is not a cosmetic issue — it directly causes ongoing cost loss for the SDK's primary workload (long agent sessions).

source_issues.title: API-key users silently stuck on 5m cache TTL: bundled CLI in v0.1.59 predates ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H opt-in
source_issues.evidence: User reports running SDK in production for 8 months, discovered during cost investigation that all cache writes billed at 5-minute tier. Reproducer shows SDK bundled CLI 2.1.105 drops ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H env var silently. Same env var works correctly on system CLI 2.1.110. Quantified impact: 'every cache write across hundreds of thousands of agent turns has been billed at the 5-minute tier'.

signals.topic: ThinkingConfig.display field not forwarded to CLI, causing Opus 4.7 thinking text to be silently empty
signals.summary: On Opus 4.7, the API changed the default thinking.display from 'summarized' to 'omitted'. The SDK's ThinkingConfig TypedDicts do not declare a 'display' field, and SubprocessCLITransport._build_command silently drops all keys except 'type', so --thinking-display never reaches the bundled CLI. All ThinkingBlock.thinking values are '' and no thinking_delta events arrive, despite the user setting thinking={'type': 'adaptive'}.
signals.review_reason: This causes key thinking content to be silently missing on a major model version. Users relying on extended thinking output receive only empty strings — this is a significant feature regression that silently degrades the output without any error. The root cause is in SDK code: the TypedDict lacks the display field and _build_command silently drops unrecognized keys.

source_issues.title: Opus 4.7 returns empty thinking text: ThinkingConfig.display not forwarded to CLI
source_issues.evidence: User provides full reproduction code showing ThinkingBlock.thinking == '' on every message for Opus 4.7 with thinking={'type': 'adaptive'}. Verified by observing signature payload size changes (424→2852 bytes) when effort is raised, confirming thinking IS happening but plaintext is hidden. Workaround requires using a hidden CLI flag via extra_args.

signals.topic: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes JavaScript renderer crash (H.reduce is not a function)
signals.summary: When a PostToolUse hook returns a valid updatedMCPToolOutput with properly shaped content, the Claude.ai web/mobile renderer crashes with 'H.reduce is not a function'. All three tool handlers on the same MCP server are reported as failed in the UI. The Python-side hook executes correctly and returns valid output — the crash is in the JavaScript rendering layer. Additionally, tool_response structure is inconsistent between documentation (dict with content key) and runtime (bare list).
signals.review_reason: This causes a UI-level crash when using a documented SDK feature (PostToolUse hooks with updatedMCPToolOutput). The renderer crash results in all tools being reported as failed, which is a critical UX breakdown — users cannot use hook-based tool normalization without breaking the session UI. Secondary issue: API/behavior mismatch between docs and runtime for tool_response shape.

source_issues.title: PostToolUse hook updatedMCPToolOutput causes H.reduce is not a function in renderer despite correct hook output
source_issues.evidence: Python hook logs show all three handlers normalize and return valid output correctly. Renderer crashes with JavaScript error 'H.reduce is not a function' in the reduce call. All three MCP tool handlers are reported as failed in the UI despite returning valid results. Secondary finding: tool_response shape differs between documentation (dict with content key) and runtime (bare list), requiring defensive isinstance checks.

signals.topic: Opus 4.7 API rejects thinking.type.enabled, error only surfaced as opaque ProcessError without SDK workaround
signals.summary: On Opus 4.7, the thinking.type.enabled value causes a 400 API error: 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported for this model. Use thinking.type.adaptive and output_config.effort'. The issue was closed but the underlying incompatibility remains — users need to know which SDK configuration works with Opus 4.7 vs earlier models.
signals.review_reason: This is an API-level rejection that blocks users from using extended thinking features on Opus 4.7. While the issue was closed (likely marked as an API/model limitation rather than SDK bug), it still represents a user-blocking scenario where the SDK does not provide clear guidance or automatic migration when targeting Opus 4.7. The error is opaque (400 without context) and the suggested fix (ThinkingConfigAdaptive) is not sufficient.

source_issues.title: Opus 4.7 + 0.1.58 = thinking.type.enabled errors?
source_issues.evidence: User receives explicit 400 API error on Opus 4.7: 'thinking.type.enabled is not supported for this model'. Error occurs with SDK and with system CLI 2.1.111. Workaround of switching to ThinkingConfigAdaptive still results in the same error, suggesting a broader compatibility gap.

signals.topic: Session resume silently drops conversation history, causing agents to lose context and duplicate side-effecting actions
signals.summary: When query() resumes a long session from JSONL, the SDK silently drops either (a) tool_use/tool_result sequences or (b) entire prior turns due to dangling parentUuid references. This causes agents to lose awareness of prior actions and re-execute them, creating duplicate database records, file uploads, and API calls.
aliases: Parent UUID dangling causes context collapse
signals.review_reason: Three distinct root causes (large-file tool pruning, dangling parentUuid, stdin premature closure) but all share the same user-facing symptom: session resume produces incomplete history, leading to agents re-executing side-effecting operations (duplicate DB records, file uploads, API calls). This is a primary-flow failure for any multi-turn agent workflow using resume. Count=3 meets the P0 threshold with clear user-visible impact (data duplication, context loss).

source_issues.title: query({resume}) silently drops tool_use/tool_result sequences from earlier turns when session JSONL grows large
source_issues.evidence: Agents lose tool_use/tool_result pairs from earlier turns while retaining user/assistant text. Observed in sessions ~1.8 MB. Result: duplicate source-add calls to external backend, duplicate notebook entries, duplicate file uploads across multiple container boots.

source_issues.title: SDK writes assistant entries with parentUuid referencing UUIDs not present in the transcript file
source_issues.evidence: SDK writes parentUuid references to UUIDs never persisted in the JSONL. Parent-chain walk stops at dangling parent on resume, collapsing entire conversation history to only the last tail. Observed after model-switch container restart: entire session context gone.

source_issues.title: SDK closes stdin after first result while CLI can continue from Monitor task-notification, causing Stream closed cascade
source_issues.evidence: SDK calls transport.endInput() after first result while CLI can still produce task-notification continuations. stdin EOF flips inputClosed flag; subsequent MCP tool calls and PostToolUse callbacks throw 'Stream closed' error. Reproduced twice in same session.

signals.topic: stdin race between initialize and first user message breaks prompt cache on Turn 2
signals.summary: The SDK's Rv function writes the first user message to CLI stdin without awaiting A.initialization, which is the promise that resolves when the CLI populates the MCP server map. When the CLI processes the user message before draining the initialize message, the first messages.create call has no MCP tools, causing tools[] to differ between Turn 1 and Turn 2, breaking Anthropic's prompt cache on Turn 2.
aliases: MCP tools missing on first turn due to unawaited init
Cache read drops from 100% to 82% due to tools[] mismatch
signals.review_reason: Cache read drops from near-100% to ~82% represents a direct cost impact: users pay significantly more per token on Turn 2+ when the prompt cache is not reused. While it is not flow-blocking, the impact is measurable and persistent. The bug is well-documented with specific reproduction steps and a one-line fix. Count=1 (single repo, single issue) so P1 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Rv writes user message without awaiting A.initialization, causing stdin race at CLI
source_issues.evidence: Observed on workloads where cache read should approach 100%, it drops to ~82% due to tools[] differing between Turn 1 and Turn 2. The fix is one line (await A.initialization) inside the Rv function. Reproduced against SDK 0.2.108 and claude-code 2.1.77 and 2.1.110.

signals.topic: Branch name validation regex rejects multiple valid git characters (#, @, non-ASCII), blocking Azure DevOps and international team workflows
signals.summary: The `validateBranchName` regex `/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9/_.-]*$/` is stricter than GitHub's actual API. It rejects `#` (Azure DevOps ticket linking), `@` (valid git branch names), and non-ASCII characters (international teams). Combined across 4 issues (751, 1024, 998, 1020), blocking entire workflow categories.
signals.review_reason: Four separate issues (count=4) all rooted in the same overly restrictive regex. Blocks entire workflow categories: Azure DevOps integration (#1024), international teams (#1020), and common git naming conventions (#998, #751). Impact is non-trivial since branch naming is decided before workflow trigger, forcing users to restructure their entire process. Sample links confirmed across all 4 issues.

signals.topic: MCP `--mcp-config` file path silently dropped when action's inline JSON config is present, breaking all custom MCP servers

The docstring promises file-path support but the implementation silently ignores it.
aliases: mergeMcpConfigs ignores file path when inline JSON present

Custom MCP servers never start, tools appear allowed but are uncallable, no error or warning is emitted. This breaks a core extensibility mechanism.

source_issues.title: --mcp-config file path in claude_args is silently dropped when action's inline JSON config is present

Root cause traced to mergeMcpConfigs conditional in base-action/src/parse-sdk-options.ts.

signals.topic: `--model` flag in `claude_args` silently ignored in tag mode, running wrong model without user awareness

aliases: tag mode model override without warning

source_issues.title: claude_args --model silently ignored in tag mode
source_issues.evidence: SDK init reports model=claude-sonnet-4-6 despite user pinning claude-haiku-4-5 via claude_args. Action's own action.yml example shows --model being set via claude_args, making this a misleading API. Users may be unknowingly running more expensive models.

signals.topic: Misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error hides orphaned/stale API key issue, causing hours of debugging
signals.summary: The Anthropic API returns identical 'Credit balance is too low' message for three distinct failure modes: actual credit depletion, model tier mismatch, and orphaned API key (valid auth but no active billing account). The orphaned-key case is especially misleading — the key authenticates, account has credits, but every request is rejected. Key rotation is the only fix.
aliases: orphaned API key misleading credit balance error
Credit balance is too low for unrelated causes
signals.review_reason: Significant UX pain: users spend hours chasing wrong root cause due to a single misleading error string masking at least 3 distinct failure modes. The orphaned-key case is particularly insidious — the key works against the API directly but fails in the action environment. Clear cost (debugging time) documented. Sample run link provided.

source_issues.title: "Credit balance is too low" returned for unrelated root causes
source_issues.evidence: ~1.5 hours debugging time across balance checks, workspace limits, tier access, and model selection before trying key rotation. Failing run shows duration_ms=187, total_cost_usd=0, is_error=true. Confirmed with direct API POST that account was healthy. Key rotation fixed it deterministically. Both GitHub repo secrets being write-only and action environment blocking secret introspection make this especially hard to diagnose.

signals.topic: `anthropic_api_key` input insufficient for Claude Code subscription; misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error

aliases: API key insufficient for Claude Code subscription
signals.review_reason: Clear credential setup pain: users with valid API keys and credits are blocked because the action requires a separate Claude Code subscription. Error is misleading (claims credit issue when account has $30). Documentation gap compounds the issue. This is a first-run blocker for new users.

source_issues.title: anthropic_api_key insufficient - misleading 'Credit balance is too low' error when Claude Code subscription required
source_issues.evidence: Fresh API key with $30 balance fails instantly with Credit balance is too low. The README documents anthropic_api_key as the auth method but does not mention it requires a Claude Code subscription. claude.ai vs platform.claude.com billing separation is unmentioned. Action docs do not clarify that claude_code_oauth_token is the correct credential for most users.

signals.topic: CLI crashes on startup with SIGILL on pre-AVX Intel CPUs (MacBookPro 9,1 / 2012 Intel Core i7)

signals.review_reason: Main flow startup crash — app is completely unusable for all users with pre-AVX Intel Macs. No workaround exists. The binary cannot run at all on affected hardware, which is a meaningful portion of the installed base (2012-2013 Intel Macs). Counts as P0 despite count=1 because the evidence shows a hard block on a real hardware segment with no path forward.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Illegal instruction (SIGILL/AVX) on Intel Core i7 MacBookPro9,1 - crashes on startup
source_issues.evidence: App binary requires AVX CPU instructions. User has MacBookPro9,1 (Mid 2012 Intel Core i7, no AVX). Crash occurs at install, before any user code runs. Exit code 4 (SIGILL). Workaround: none. The user explicitly states 'this never worked' and 'no last working version'.

signals.topic: Recursive 'claude doctor' call from Bash tool inside active Windows session crashes the entire Claude Code process
signals.summary: Invoking 'claude doctor' via the Bash tool from within an active Claude Code session causes immediate and complete process termination on Windows. The session ends with no error message, no graceful shutdown, and no recovery option.
aliases: process terminates when claude doctor run from session
signals.review_reason: Active session state crash — running a diagnostic command inside a session causes complete session termination with no recovery path. This is a direct user workflow blocker on Windows, a major platform. The bug is labeled 'has repro' with explicit repro steps and a plausible root cause hypothesis.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Running `claude doctor` via Bash tool inside active session crashes Claude Code (Windows)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed with repro steps on Windows 11. Running 'claude doctor 2>&1' from Bash tool inside active session causes immediate session termination. No error message, no log entry, no recovery. Related issue #37723 (same command, different platform). signals.topic: Automated duplicate-detection bot systematically auto-closes legitimate issues at scale without human review

aliases: bot auto-closes bugs without human review
signals.review_reason: Systematic silencing of user feedback at scale — 15,240 issues affected, 10%+ false positive rate means ~1,500 unique bug reports and feature requests silently killed. Critical data loss and security reports are being auto-closed with the same keyword matching as feature requests, with no human review. This directly undermines the issue tracker as a feedback channel.

source_issues.title: Duplicate detection bot is auto-closing valid issues at scale — 15,240 closures and counting
source_issues.evidence: 15,240 issues auto-closed by the bot. Specific false positive examples cited: #46572 (user explicitly wrote 'NOT A DUPLICATE' in title, still closed), #48499 (bot-generated prompt submitted as issue, closed as duplicate of another bot-closed issue), #50846 (CRITICAL BUG about data loss auto-closed as duplicate), #50870 (architecture proposal closed as duplicate of bug reports). signals.topic: Voice mode spontaneously activates mid-session despite both voiceEnabled and voice.enabled set to false in settings.json

source_issues.title: telegram plugin: orphan watchdog false-positives on bun reparenting — plugin self-terminates every ~5s

source_issues.title: Bug: telegram plugin's MCP server spins at 100% CPU indefinitely after parent Claude Code session exits
source_issues.evidence: Same ppid-based orphan watchdog failed in a different scenario: bun run wrapper outlived Claude Code, ppid stayed valid from PID 1's perspective, stdin never closed, SIGTERM ignored due to event loop saturation. signals.topic: skills update command silently fails on Windows when Node.js path contains spaces
signals.summary: On Windows with default Node.js installation (e.g. C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe), `npx skills update` silently fails with no actionable error message. aliases: Windows skills update failure with Program Files
skills update silent failure on Windows
signals.review_reason: This is a blocking failure for the skills update workflow on Windows, which is a common installation scenario (Program Files is the default Node.js install path). source_issues.title: [Bug] skills update fails on Windows when Node.js path contains spaces

User sees only '✗ Failed to update <skill-name>' with no actionable details. Reproduction confirmed on Windows 11 with Node.js v25.6.0 at default install path.

signals.topic: skill-creator eval loop blocks the entire Claude session for minutes with no progress feedback

signals.review_reason: This creates a severe UX degradation where users see their Claude session freeze for extended periods (minutes) with zero feedback. A crashed or hung eval loop is completely invisible to users, meaning they cannot distinguish between a stuck process and normal long-running operation. This is a workflow-blocking experience issue even though it does not cause data loss.

source_issues.evidence: User waits minutes during eval with no progress feedback. run_loop.py blocks in a single Bash call. Description optimization iteration takes 30-60 seconds each. signals.topic: Context auto-compaction fails and renders session unrecoverable even when context is not actually exhausted

aliases: Token count miscalculation triggers premature compaction
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked — the session enters an unrecoverable state. Compaction is Goose's core mechanism for handling long conversations; when it fails, the entire session is dead. Evidence is explicit and corroborated by multiple linked historical issues. Count=1 is justified by exceptionally strong user impact (unrecoverable, affects even new sessions) and explicit root cause documentation.

source_issues.title: Context limit reached + compaction failure on sessions that haven't exceeded context

signals.topic: Codex API returns empty response, blocking the core summarization workflow
signals.summary: When using fabric with the codex (ChatGPT) backend, the LLM returns an empty response, causing the entire summarization workflow to fail with no output. This is a complete flow blockage — the primary use case of summarizing content is broken for codex users.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary flow blockage. The user runs the core CLI command (fabric summarize via codex backend) and receives zero output. Although count=1, the severity is critical because: (1) it completely blocks the main summarization workflow, (2) it appears to be an API/backend compatibility issue that likely affects all codex users, and (3) empty response bugs in LLM integrations are notoriously underreported as users often attribute failures to API keys or quotas rather than the tool itself.

signals.topic: Missing LICENSE file blocks institutional adoption and automated compliance checks

signals.topic: Dataset shard cache lacks integrity verification — silent data corruption risk

aliases: No cache integrity check in prepare.py
Cached dataset shards not verified before reuse
signals.review_reason: Lack of cache integrity verification creates a real risk of silent data corruption during training. While not confirmed as a widespread active breakage, the scenario is explicitly described as dangerous in shared/distributed environments and the proposed fix is straightforward. source_issues.title: Harden downloaded dataset shard cache in prepare.py

signals.topic: ShellSession.execute() hangs and times out when shell command output lacks trailing newline
signals.summary: ShellSession uses line.startswith(marker) to detect command completion, but when a command's output doesn't end with \n, the done-marker gets concatenated to the last output line, causing startswith() to fail and execute() to hang until timeout.
signals.review_reason: Verified reproducible bug with a complete repro script. ShellSession.execute() is a core agent execution primitive. The bug causes timeouts on extremely common shell patterns (echo -n, printf, file content without trailing newline), directly blocking agent shell execution workflows. Not P0 only because count=1 and single-repository.

source_issues.title: ShellSession times out when command output lacks trailing newline due to marker concatenation

signals.topic: Symlink-based relative path in prompt loader allows reading unintended files (TOCTOU path traversal)
signals.summary: load_prompt_from_config resolves relative paths and follows symlinks without validating the final resolved target, allowing an attacker who can modify symlinks to read arbitrary files the application did not intend to load.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) path traversal vulnerability in langchain-core's prompt loader. The loader validates the user-provided path string but not the symlink-resolved final target. An attacker with filesystem write access can redirect file reads to sensitive locations. Reporter explicitly documents the security impact and provides reproduction steps. Single-issue but clear, severe user impact (arbitrary file read).

source_issues.title: Symlink-Based File Read via Relative Path in LangChain Core Prompt Loader
source_issues.evidence: Reporter provides step-by-step repro: create symlink pointing to normal.txt, load config with relative path 'link.txt', then change symlink target to secret.txt — same path now reads different content. Application cannot enforce allowlist on resolved file path. Security impact: if attacker can influence filesystem state (e.g. writable directories), they can make the app read arbitrary files.

signals.review_reason: Quantified performance regression: ~300-500ms added to every application startup when importing BaseChatModel, even for users who never use HuggingFace models. Root cause is a single top-level import in langchain-core. Impact is diffuse (every user pays the cost) but not blocking. Count=1, single-repo, non-blocking — P2.

source_issues.title: Performance: transformers are imported unconditionally on BaseChatModel import

signals.topic: Long tool calls (~3+ min) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing duplicate LLM calls and 2-3x cost
signals.summary: On LangGraph Cloud, tool calls running longer than ~180 seconds are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both complete successfully, resulting in duplicate LLM invocations and 2-3x cost overruns. The root cause is in the background job sweep mechanism (BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 hardcoded, sweep runs every 240s) which incorrectly marks active runs as stale.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed production-breaking issue causing direct financial harm: 2-3x cost overruns from duplicate LLM calls. Both the original and duplicate tool executions complete successfully, meaning users are billed twice for the same work. The user has traced the root cause to the hardcoded BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT=120 and the 240s sweep interval in the Go persistence server. All workarounds (env vars) are ineffective, indicating a platform-level bug. Severity is elevated by being on a managed cloud platform where users cannot modify the server-side behavior.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: User reports on LangGraph Cloud (EU, Plus tier, langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6) that tool calls taking 3-10 minutes are silently re-dispatched at ~180s. Both original and duplicate complete successfully. Environment variable workarounds (BG_JOB_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_PERIOD_SECS=900, BG_JOB_ISOLATED_LOOPS=true) have no effect. BG_JOB_HEARTBEAT is hardcoded at 120 in langgraph-api config/__init__.py. Related to #6726 (CancelledError not caught) and #5672 (streamed state loss on cancel).

signals.topic: Run cancellation causes loss of streamed state that has not yet been persisted as a checkpoint
signals.summary: When a LangGraph run is cancelled during streaming, the most recent in-progress streamed state is not persisted to the checkpoint database. Any streamed output the user saw is lost upon resumption or sync — the backend only reflects the last completed checkpoint, not the full streamed state.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed session state loss bug that directly impacts user experience: users see streamed output for seconds or longer, but all of it disappears after cancellation and sync. This creates an inconsistent, surprising UX for any streaming chat application. The user provides a clear technical root cause (checkpointing only on full run completion, not on cancel events) and a feature proposal. The issue affects both dev and cloud deployments and is marked 'bug' by the reporter. This is NOT a cosmetic issue — it results in permanent data loss from the user's perspective.

source_issues.title: Run Cancellation Causes Loss of Streamed State Not Yet Persisted as a Checkpoint
source_issues.evidence: User describes: (1) start a streaming LangGraph run, (2) cancel before completion, (3) send new message causing frontend to sync with backend, (4) all streamed data since the last checkpoint is missing. The user explicitly identifies the root cause: 'checkpointing only happens at full run/task completion, not on cancel/abort/stream end events.' Mentions this affects both dev and cloud deployments. Provides technical insight that 'there is no mechanism for a flush/persist to checkpoint right now on cancel/disconnect.' Related to #7417 via shared cancellation handling code path.

signals.topic: PostgreSQL checkpointer stores partial graph state under inconsistent thread_id formats, causing data loss on retrieval
signals.summary: When using PostgreSQL as the checkpointer storage, after an interruption occurs, the checkpoint_writes table contains two forms of thread_id: one as a plain string and another in hexadecimal-encoded form. Retrieving state with the string-form thread_id misses data stored under the hex-encoded form, resulting in incomplete state restoration.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed data integrity bug in the PostgreSQL checkpointer that causes partial state loss. The user provides a complete reproducible example with a live database trace showing the same logical thread_id stored in two different encoding formats. State channels critical for resume (like __interrupt__ and __resume__) are present only under the hex-encoded form, making proper state recovery impossible. This directly breaks human-in-the-loop workflows and any interrupt-based approval process using PostgresSaver.

source_issues.title: Partial Graph State Missing Due to Mixed thread_id Formats in checkpoint_writes
source_issues.evidence: User provides full database trace showing the same thread_id ('approval-123') stored in two different forms in the checkpoint_writes table, with some state channels present only under the hex-encoded form. On retrieval using the string form, those channels are absent. Includes a complete minimal reproducible example using PostgresSaver, interrupt(), Command(resume=True), and a database trace showing the format inconsistency. Reproducible on Windows with langgraph 1.0.4.

signals.topic: MongoDB checkpointer serde/msgpack fails when state contains BSON ObjectId types, preventing checkpoint persistence
signals.summary: When using MongoDB checkpointing and state contains BSON ObjectId types (common in MongoDB-backed applications), the JsonPlusSerializer and msgpack encoder both raise TypeError because ObjectId is not natively JSON-serializable and is not handled by the msgpack encoder.
aliases: MongoDB ObjectId not JSON serializable in checkpointer
signals.review_reason: This is a blocking bug for MongoDB users: any state containing ObjectId (the standard MongoDB document ID type) cannot be checkpointed. Both JSON and msgpack serialization paths fail. The user's application state inherently contains ObjectIds (since it's a MongoDB-backed app), making the checkpointer completely non-functional for their use case. There is no workaround without manually patching internal methods. This defeats the core persistence guarantee of the checkpointer for the entire MongoDB user segment.

source_issues.title: ObjectId handling by msgpack in MongoDb checkpointer
source_issues.evidence: User provides a minimal repro showing a Pydantic model with ObjectId field fails serialization in both JsonPlusSerializer.dumps() (TypeError: ObjectId is not JSON serializable) and _msgpack_enc() (also fails). User notes langgraph does not bundle bson as a dependency, making ObjectId handling the checkpointer's responsibility. This is a fundamental incompatibility that prevents MongoDB checkpointer from working for any state containing ObjectId — which is the standard MongoDB document ID type and is ubiquitous in MongoDB-backed apps.

signals.topic: langgraph 1.1.7 regression: OpenTelemetry instrumentation causes TypeError crash at agent invocation time
signals.summary: A regression introduced in langgraph 1.1.7 (via PR #7429, graph lifecycle callbacks feature) causes a TypeError crash when LangGraph agents are used with opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain. The new strict handler type checking in _GraphCallbackManager rejects the TraceloopCallbackHandler from OpenTelemetry instrumentation, crashing the agent at invocation time.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression that breaks a production-critical integration: any LangGraph deployment using OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation (standard in AWS Bedrock AgentCore and many observability setups) crashes at invocation time in langgraph 1.1.7. The crash is a TypeError (not caught exception), making the agent completely non-functional. Since the crash occurs at invoke time (not deploy time), it bypasses pre-deployment validation and surfaces in production. The regression was introduced by a feature PR (#7429) and the user has identified two concrete fix approaches. Severity is elevated by the AWS Bedrock AgentCore production impact.

source_issues.title: langgraph 1.1.7 regression: TypeError with opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain
source_issues.evidence: Introduced by PR #7429 in 1.1.7 (1.1.6 was fine). When opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain is active, the new strict add_handler() type check in _GraphCallbackManager rejects TraceloopCallbackHandler (which inherits BaseCallbackHandler, not GraphCallbackHandler) with 'TypeError: handlers must inherit GraphCallbackHandler'. Full stack trace provided. Affects AWS Bedrock AgentCore deployments which rely on aws-opentelemetry-distro for auto-instrumentation. User notes 'deploys succeed — crash only surfaces at invocation time,' making it a production blocker that bypasses pre-deployment checks.

signals.topic: OAuth/API Key configuration modals are hidden behind account settings dialog due to incorrect z-index

signals.review_reason: This is a UI interaction bug that completely blocks the data source OAuth/API key authentication workflow. The modal is rendered behind the dialog making it inaccessible. Root cause is clearly identified in the issue (z-index mismatch). Blocks plugin/data source configuration.

source_issues.evidence: OAuthClientSettings and ApiKeyModal set wrapperClassName='z-1002!' which is lower than account settings dialog wrapper (z-9998). Modal renders behind dialog and is completely inaccessible.

aliases: workflow python code execution blocked docker
signals.review_reason: Python code execution in workflows is a core feature that is broken on self-hosted Docker deployments. This blocks any workflow using code nodes. The user must manually rebuild the sandbox container, indicating a missing dependency or misconfiguration in the Docker image.

signals.topic: parse_vision_messages crashes with AttributeError when message content is array type and vision is disabled
signals.summary: Memory.add() calls parse_vision_messages() without passing an LLM when enable_vision=False (the default). The function defaults to llm=None and unconditionally calls llm.generate_response() for list-typed or image_url-dict content, causing AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'generate_response'. Standard multimodal message formats from OpenAI SDK and LangChain trigger this crash.
aliases: list content type crash in Memory.add
signals.review_reason: Memory.add() crashes on standard OpenAI SDK multimodal message formats when vision is disabled (the default). Two independent reporters confirm the same crash path. This breaks the primary user-facing API for anyone using standard LLM SDKs. The fix is trivial (add None check before llm call), but the impact is wide since list-typed content is the standard format from modern LLM frameworks.

source_issues.title: fix: AttributeError crash in Memory.add() when message content is a list and vision is disabled
source_issues.evidence: parse_vision_messages defaults llm=None. When enable_vision=False, Memory.add() calls it without passing LLM. List content and image_url dict branches unconditionally call llm.generate_response() without checking if llm is None. Standard OpenAI SDK multimodal message format triggers this.

source_issues.title: parse_vision_messages fails to work correctly when encountering an array content
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed in AsyncMemory with messages containing list-typed content (standard OpenAI format). Crash occurs in parse_vision_messages. Two independent reporters with the same root cause.

signals.topic: Memory extraction pipeline produces ~97% junk data with hallucination feedback loop amplification
signals.summary: In a 32-day production audit of 10,134 entries, 97.8% were junk including hallucinated user profiles, boot-file restating, system noise, and transient state. Extracted facts go straight to vector store with no quality gate. Recalled memories re-enter extraction, causing 808 copies of a single hallucination. Better models worsen the problem by following the permissive extraction prompt more faithfully.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency in production impact (97.8% junk), confirmed across two extraction models over 32 days. Feedback loop causes indefinite hallucination amplification (808 copies of one fabricated fact). No quality gate means every extracted fact is stored, directly contradicting the product's core value. Users invested 32 days before discovering the scale of the problem.

source_issues.title: What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk
source_issues.evidence: 32-day production audit with 10,134 entries. 97.8% junk rate across two extraction models. Root causes: no quality gate between extraction and storage, feedback loop where recalled memories re-enter extraction unflagged, no negative few-shot examples in extraction prompt, no REJECT action in update decision, no identity-aware extraction.

signals.topic: Claude plugin OAuth access_token not refreshed on expiry — forces full re-authentication every ~hour

The refresh_token stored in ~/.claude/.credentials.json is never used to silently mint a new access_token. Instead, Claude Code re-exposes only the two authenticate tools instead of the 11 real Mem0 MCP tools, making the integration unusable for daily work.
aliases: Claude Code integration broken after token expiry
signals.review_reason: Key feature (Claude Code integration) becomes completely non-functional after ~1 hour. No workaround within the plugin — only an external config bypass exists. Blocks daily workflow. While count=1, the impact is severe (full feature unavailability every hour) and is the primary integration point for Claude Code users.

source_issues.title: [claude-plugin] OAuth access_token not refreshed when expired — plugin falls back to re-authentication instead of using stored refresh_token
source_issues.evidence: Plugin exposes 11 authenticated MCP tools initially; after token expiry only 2 auth tools remain. User forced through browser OAuth flow roughly every hour. Direct server queries prove server is healthy — failure is entirely on client-side token lifecycle. ~/.claude/mcp-needs-auth-cache.json shows stale entry after expiry.

signals.topic: SQL/Cypher injection in PGVector, Azure MySQL, and Neptune Analytics vector stores via collection_name and filters
signals.summary: Same injection class previously fixed for Databricks in PR #4558 was left unpatched in PGVector, Azure MySQL, and Neptune Analytics. PGVector has 18 injection points, Azure MySQL 11, Neptune 2+ with additional user-controlled filter value injection in Cypher queries. Neptune does not require authentication for the /configure endpoint when ADMIN_API_KEY is not set.
signals.review_reason: Incomplete fix of a known vulnerability class leaves 3 vector store backends exposed. Neptune's unauthenticated /search endpoint accepts user-controlled filter values that flow directly to Cypher queries. Demonstrated attack path for full table DROP via PoC. While no confirmed in-wild exploitation, the attack surface is clear and the fix from Databricks is available but not applied. User impact: potential complete data destruction for Neptune deployments.

source_issues.title: [Security] SQL/Cypher Injection in PGVector, Azure MySQL, and Neptune vector stores via collection_name (CWE-89)
source_issues.evidence: 18 injection points in PGVector, 11 in Azure MySQL, Neptune has both collection_name and user-controlled filter value injection in Cypher WHERE clause. /configure endpoint is unauthenticated when ADMIN_API_KEY is not set. Full PoC provided for DROP TABLE and UNION-based data exfiltration. CVSS 8.1 for Neptune, 6.5 for PGVector/MySQL. Prior art: same bug class fixed for Databricks in #4073/#4558 but 3 backends not patched.

signals.topic: BM25 keyword search and entity extraction silently degrade to no-op for all non-English languages
signals.summary: v3 hybrid search pipeline hardcodes spaCy's en_core_web_sm model for BM25 lemmatization and entity extraction. CJK, Arabic, Thai, Hindi, and other non-Latin script users get zero BM25 signal and zero entity boost. The degradation is completely silent — no error is raised, search simply returns results as if BM25 did not exist.
signals.review_reason: Major feature (v3 hybrid search) silently broken for the majority of the global user base. The silent nature is the worst UX — users don't know their results are degraded, they just get worse precision on exact-match queries like Chinese employee IDs or Japanese names. This is a core feature regression for all non-English deployments.

source_issues.title: BM25 keyword search and entity extraction are hardcoded to English
source_issues.evidence: spacy.load('en_core_web_sm') hardcoded in two places for entity extraction and lemmatization. CJK tokenization produces no meaningful units. bm25_scores returns empty, has_bm25 set to False silently. Entity boost disappears. Net effect: hybrid pipeline degrades to semantic-only for all non-English. No error raised — users just miss precision improvements. Workaround exists but is undocumented.

signals.topic: .NET dynamic tool activation mid-run fails: stale ChatOptions.Tools snapshot causes 'Function not found' after activate_tools
signals.summary: Two related bugs block the dynamic tooling pattern (bootstrapping a tool subset, then activating more tools mid-run via a model call): (1) ChatOptions.Clone() copies the Tools list by reference, so after activate_tools mutates the live list, outer layers may hold a cloned ChatOptions with a stale tool list reference, causing FunctionInvokingChatClient to resolve against the old list and return FunctionInvocationStatus.NotFound; (2) middleware path for ChatOptions.Tools refresh was unreliable. These bugs make the dynamic tooling pattern unusable in practice.
aliases: dynamic tooling Function not found mid-run
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues both demonstrating that the dynamic tool activation pattern is broken in the current .NET SDK — a core extensibility feature. Users cannot reliably activate tools mid-run, forcing them into workarounds. Count=2 with two distinct bug reports providing strong evidence.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: ChatOptions.Tools snapshot vs in-place mutation mid-run; FunctionInvocationResult vs exceptions (dynamic tooling)
source_issues.evidence: After activate_tools succeeds, a subsequent model tool_calls for a newly activated function sometimes fails with 'Function not found' (FunctionInvocationStatus.NotFound). Logs show ChatOptions.Tools count still matching an older snapshot because ChatOptions.Clone() copied the Tools collection by reference.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: ChatClientAgent + dynamic ChatOptions.Tools: middleware ordering vs plugin-time refresh; FunctionInvokingChatClient wrapping and IncludeDetailedErrors
source_issues.evidence: Refreshing ChatOptions.Tools after activate_tools via middleware path was unreliable — model still received 'Function not found' for just-activated tools. Workaround: refresh the in-place list inside the plugin itself. Also: FunctionInvokingChatClient needs IncludeDetailedErrors=true for consistent tool failure surfacing.

signals.topic: .NET Checkpoint serialization loses ToolCall concrete type, silently breaking HITL/FICC approval resume
signals.summary: When ToolApprovalRequestContent is persisted via JsonCheckpointStore and restored, its ToolCall property reverts from concrete FunctionCallContent to abstract base ToolCallContent. This causes FunctionInvokingChatClient.ExtractAndRemoveApprovalRequestsAndResponses to silently skip the approval TARC — the call id is never added to approvalRequestCallIds and the downstream approval logic is bypassed. No error is raised, making the bug invisible to users.
signals.review_reason: HITL/FICC approval is a core enterprise safety mechanism. When checkpoint restore silently bypasses the approval check rather than raising an error, users are unaware that automated tool calls are proceeding without human review — a critical trust/security regression. Not P0 because count=1 single repo.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: Checkpoint round-trip loses `ToolApprovalRequestContent.ToolCall` concrete type (`FunctionCallContent` → base `ToolCallContent`), breaking FICC approval resume
source_issues.evidence: TARC is silently skipped in FunctionInvokingChatClient.ExtractAndRemoveApprovalRequestsAndResponses; call id never added to approvalRequestCallIds; downstream validation/invocation does not handle approval. Root cause identified as System.Text.Json requiring polymorphic metadata for abstract base properties during round-trip.

signals.topic: .NET RunStreamingAsync throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException with tools: 'Unknown ChatToolCallKind value'
signals.summary: When using tools and streaming via RunStreamingAsync, an ArgumentOutOfRangeException is thrown intermittently with message 'Unknown ChatToolCallKind value. (Parameter 'value') Actual value was .' — an empty string value. This is a main flow blocker for streaming tool-calling use cases.
signals.review_reason: Direct main flow crash during streaming tool execution — ArgumentOutOfRangeException thrown from the framework's core streaming path (FunctionInvokingChatClient.GetStreamingResponseAsync). While described as 'occasional', any unhandled exception in the streaming path blocks the user's streaming pipeline. P0 justified as main flow blocking with clear stack trace evidence.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: An exception is thrown when using tool and calling RunStreamingAsync.
source_issues.evidence: Sporadic ArgumentOutOfRangeException thrown at OpenAI.Chat.ChatToolCallKindExtensions.ToChatToolCallKind with empty string value, propagated through Microsoft.Extensions.AI.FunctionInvokingChatClient.GetStreamingResponseAsync. Affects Microsoft.Agents.AI 1.1.0 and Microsoft.Agents.AI.OpenAI 1.1.0 on .NET 10.

signals.topic: Python AG-UI protocol violations: reasoning role hardcoded as 'assistant' instead of 'reasoning', multimodal media parsed from wrong field
signals.summary: The agent-framework Python AG-UI implementation violates the AG-UI specification in two ways: (1) reasoning messages use role 'assistant' instead of 'reasoning', so thinking/thinking-content messages do not render correctly in AG-UI-compatible clients; (2) _parse_multimodal_media_part reads field 'data' instead of the spec-required 'value' field, so all multimodal user input (images, files) is silently dropped and invisible to AI agents behind AG-UI endpoints.
signals.review_reason: Protocol specification violations that cause complete functional failure: (1) reasoning messages are invisible to all spec-compliant AG-UI clients — users lose access to the thinking/reasoning feature entirely; (2) ALL multimodal user input is silently dropped — a complete data loss for image/file interactions. Both are critical AG-UI feature kills with direct code line references proving the bug.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: AG-UI reasoning and multimodal media parsing doesn't correctly follow the specification
source_issues.evidence: Code reference: _run_common.py lines 599 and 616 hardcode 'assistant' role for reasoning messages; _message_adapters.py line 266 parses 'data' field instead of 'value' per spec. Both violations cause complete failure of the respective feature when clients conform to the AG-UI specification.

signals.topic: Python MCPStreamableHTTPTool background SSE notification failure crashes the entire agent run
signals.summary: MCPStreamableHTTPTool always spawns a background GET / Accept: text/event-stream task for the MCP notification channel. When this background task fails — which happens predictably on major MCP providers (Microsoft Learn API returns 405 Method Not Allowed; D365 F&O silently hangs/resets) — the exception propagates through TaskGroup and cancels the entire agent run, making the entire agent unusable even though the primary tool call may have succeeded.
signals.review_reason: Predictable MCP provider behavior (returning 405 on a GET that the framework always sends) causes entire agent run cancellation — a disproportionate failure mode where a background notification failure destroys a successful primary tool call. Users cannot use the framework with real-world MCP providers without a fix. Not P0 because workaround exists (don't use affected MCP providers) and count=1.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: MCPStreamableHTTPTool background notification stream (GET SSE) failure crashes entire agent (405 on Learn MCP + connection failure on D365 F&O)
source_issues.evidence: Background TaskGroup exception from MCPStreamableHTTPTool notification channel propagates and cancels the whole agent run. Confirmed on two major MCP providers: Microsoft Learn MCP (405), D365 F&O MCP (hang/reset). Suggested fix: make notification failure non-fatal and update to Streamable HTTP transport.

Users passing invalid participants (None, wrong types, non-agent objects) encounter opaque AttributeError/TypeError instead of a descriptive validation error. source_issues.title: RoundRobinGroupChat raises raw AttributeError/TypeError for invalid participants instead of a clear validation error

signals.topic: SelectorGroupChat livelock: allow_repeated_speaker=False fallback returns excluded previous speaker, causing infinite conversation loops
signals.summary: SelectorGroupChat falls back to returning the previous speaker when max_selector_attempts is exhausted, even when allow_repeated_speaker=False is set, causing agents to loop forever in group chats.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed livelock bug that causes multi-agent conversations to hang indefinitely. The fallback logic in _selector_group_chat.py explicitly returns the excluded previous speaker, violating the allow_repeated_speaker=False contract. This is a main-flow blocking bug that renders group chat unusable in production when the LLM consistently selects the previous speaker.

source_issues.title: [Bug] SelectorGroupChat livelock: fallback returns excluded previous speaker when allow_repeated_speaker=False
source_issues.evidence: When allow_repeated_speaker=False and the LLM selector fails to pick a valid speaker within max_selector_attempts, the fallback logic returns self._previous_speaker — the exact speaker that was supposed to be excluded. This creates a livelock: Agent A speaks → selector fails → falls back to A → A speaks again → repeat forever.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code on the host without sandboxing; only a UserWarning is issued, trivially suppressed in production environments
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a local subprocess with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions; the only safeguard is a UserWarning easily suppressed in production, leading to arbitrary code execution on the host machine.
signals.review_reason: Critical security vulnerability with clear user impact: arbitrary code execution with host privileges when LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor is used. The only safeguard (UserWarning) is trivially suppressible in production, meaning following the existing quickstart docs can result in full system compromise. This maps to OWASP ASI-09 and CWE-94. Users deploying AutoGen in production following standard examples are exposed to credential theft and system takeover.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code directly to disk and executes it as a local subprocess via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions. The only safeguard is a UserWarning at construction time which is silently swallowed in most production configurations (e.g., -W ignore, logging pipelines). An attacker or prompt-injected LLM can execute arbitrary code with full host privileges, leading to credential theft, lateral movement, and data destruction.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Firefox never exits on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Firefox hangs forever on Windows with non-graceful exit. Expected 30s teardown never occurs. Process becomes zombie, blocking automation pipelines.

signals.topic: Expect assertions with escalating retry intervals skip final DOM check before timeout deadline
signals.summary: Locator assertions (toBeVisible, toHaveText, etc.) using retry intervals [100, 250, 500, 1000] can skip the final DOM check before the timeout deadline fires, causing assertions to fail even when the element is already visible — wasting up to 999ms of timeout budget.
aliases: toBeVisible false negative due to retry scheduling
signals.review_reason: 核心断言 API 的逻辑缺陷：retryWithProgressAndTimeouts 在 deadline 触发时不执行最后一次 DOM 检查，导致所有 locator 断言（toBeVisible、toHaveText 等）在元素已出现的情况下仍然超时失败。引发大量误报式测试失败，严重破坏测试可靠性。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Expect assertions with escalating retry intervals skip final check before deadline, wasting up to 1000ms of timeout budget
source_issues.evidence: Precise reproduction case provided. Root cause identified in retryWithProgressAndTimeouts in frames.ts. All locator assertions affected: toBeVisible, toBeHidden, toContainText, toHaveText, etc. Element visible 600ms before deadline but assertion times out.

signals.topic: Reasoning/thinking content from LLM providers is not represented in ChatMessage abstraction, causing data loss
signals.summary: LLM providers (Ollama, OpenAI reasoning models, etc.) return structured reasoning/thinking data that Semantic Kernel's ChatMessage abstraction cannot represent, resulting in loss of useful model output and inconsistent provider behavior. Users must rely on provider-specific parsing via RawRepresentation.
signals.review_reason: Two independent issue reports (#13889, #13860) both document that reasoning/thinking output from LLM providers is lost or missing in Semantic Kernel's ChatMessage abstraction. Issue #13860 is labeled 'bug' with a screenshot and 10 comments confirming the problem. Issue #13889 details the root cause: no standardized content type for reasoning data across providers. signals.topic: Async Responses structured outputs memory leak — unbounded SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer allocation on every parse() call
signals.summary: Using AsyncResponses.parse() with Pydantic models causes a memory leak. The root cause is that ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] uses a free module-level TypeVar that Pydantic cannot resolve, causing model_rebuild() to always return False. This prevents caching in MockCoreSchema._built_memo, so a new heavy Rust SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer is allocated on every single parse() call and accumulates without bound.
signals.review_reason: Memory leak causing unbounded Rust object allocation is a severe production reliability issue. A long-running server using responses.parse() will progressively consume memory until OOM crash. The issue has a complete root cause analysis with a flame graph and a precise code-level explanation. This is not a theoretical edge case — it affects every production deployment using async structured outputs.

At scale (millions of requests, ~700 workers), this causes significant production failures.

With hundreds of workers processing millions of requests, even a 0.6% failure rate represents thousands of failed requests. The issue has a detailed root cause analysis and reproducible conditions, making it a clear user pain point.

aliases: report flow incorrectly flags skill as suspicious
signals.review_reason: Count=2 covering three distinct but related platform failures. The search/indexing staleness directly degrades skill discoverability — a core platform function. The metadata refresh failure means published content is misrepresented. The most severe is the in-product report flow incorrectly flagging the reporting author's own skill as suspicious, creating a direct negative consequence for using platform feedback tools. Issue #1733 corroborates the suspicious flag problem. Combined, these represent systemic failures in the publish → discover → feedback loop.

source_issues.title: Search does not recall ip-publisher, summary not refreshed after v1.0.5, and report flow flagged the skill as suspicious

signals.topic: GitHub OAuth endpoint /api/auth/signin/github returns HTTP 500 — all authenticated CLI operations blocked
signals.summary: The GitHub OAuth sign-in endpoint returns HTTP 500 on both the Vercel frontend and Convex backend. This completely breaks `clawhub login` — no new authentication tokens can be generated. All authenticated operations (publish, whoami, sync) are blocked. Only read-only operations (search, explore, inspect) remain functional.
aliases: no new tokens can be generated
signals.review_reason: Single issue but extremely high severity: complete auth flow breakage for GitHub OAuth, affecting every new user attempting to authenticate. The evidence includes direct curl confirmation of HTTP 500 from two independent endpoints. The blocked operations (publish, whoami, sync) are core platform workflows. The root cause (expired/missing GitHub OAuth app credentials) is a single-point infrastructure failure with no user-side workaround.

source_issues.title: Bug: /api/auth/signin/github returns HTTP 500 — GitHub OAuth broken, no new tokens can be generated

signals.topic: /api/v1/skills list endpoint returns empty items array for all callers — CLI explore command non-functional

The official `clawhub@0.9.0` CLI `explore` command hits this endpoint and prints 'No skills found.' for all users. The issue reproduces across all query parameters and sort options. The sibling endpoint `/api/v1/search` works fine on the same token, confirming auth is not the cause.
signals.review_reason: Count=1 but high user impact: the official CLI explore command is completely non-functional for all users. The evidence is extremely detailed with curl tables showing byte-identical empty responses across all auth states. The sibling `/api/v1/search` working confirms this is a specific server-side bug in the catalog-list endpoint rather than an auth or quota issue. This is a platform-level breakage of the skill discovery workflow.

source_issues.title: `/api/v1/skills` returns empty `{items:[]}` for all callers — `clawhub explore` affected
source_issues.evidence: Comprehensive table showing identical 30-byte empty response across anonymous, invalid-token, and valid-token requests. Official CLI explore command returns 'No skills found.' Sibling search endpoint works. Rate limit not exhausted. Demonstrates server-side bug via byte-identical response.

signals.topic: Publish form rejects valid semver minor/major version bumps — skill maintainers forced to misuse patch bumps
signals.summary: The publish-new-version form auto-populates the version field with a patch bump (e.g. 1.5.1 → 1.5.2), which is accepted. However, any manual edit to change the version to a minor or major bump (e.g. 1.6.0, 2.0.0) triggers a client-side validation error 'Version must be valid semver (e.g. 1.0.0)' even though the entered value is valid semver. The error message is misleading — it implies a format issue when the actual rule is a hidden patch-only check. This forces maintainers to either misuse patch bumps or bypass the web UI entirely.
aliases: cannot publish minor major releases from web UI
signals.review_reason: Single issue but significant workflow impact: skill maintainers cannot publish semver-compliant minor or major releases from the web UI. The issue includes clear reproduction steps, root cause hypothesis, and a documented workaround that introduces incorrect version metadata in the registry. The misleading error message ('must be valid semver') causes users to waste time trying format variants that cannot work because the actual rule is hidden. This breaks semantic versioning semantics for the entire skill ecosystem.

source_issues.title: Publish skill page: version field rejects valid minor/major bumps with 'must be valid semver' error
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction steps with specific version examples. Root cause analysis suggests validator checks equality with auto-populated value rather than validating semver format. Workaround forces patch bump misuse. Error message misleads users into trying v1.6.0, v1.6, etc. User is publishing v1.6.0 content as 1.5.2 to work around the bug.

This is a complete main-flow block — users cannot get any agent response at all.

All three issues share the identical root error 'incomplete turn detected payloads=0' across different user environments (clean Ubuntu, macOS onboarding, existing workspace). Each represents a complete main-flow block — users receive zero agent responses regardless of message content or interface used (UI, Telegram, Dashboard). This is the highest-impact pain point in the dataset.

signals.topic: Slack tool results leak as individual messages despite verbose/block-streaming disabled
signals.summary: Tool execution outputs (exec stdout/stderr, JSON dumps) are delivered as separate Slack messages in channels even when the user has explicitly disabled verbose output and block streaming in config. aliases: tool output not suppressed in Slack channels
signals.review_reason: Data leakage with clear user impact: users who explicitly configured verbose=off and block streaming still receive raw tool output in Slack channels. source_issues.title: Slack channel tool results leak despite verboseDefault=off and block streaming disabled
source_issues.evidence: Tool results (exec stdout/stderr, JSON dumps) are delivered as individual Slack messages in channels even when config fully disables verbose/block streaming. signals.topic: Uncaught symlink loop error crashes file traversal during repo map generation

This is a known edge case in pathlib usage that should be handled gracefully with a warning rather than a crash.

signals.topic: Multiple hooks/session commands hang indefinitely after completing work — process never exits
signals.summary: ruflo hooks post-task, hooks session-end, and session save all complete their core work but then hang indefinitely because the Node.js process never exits. Some non-daemon handle (timer, watcher, IPC socket, pending Promise) keeps the event loop alive after the recorded outcome is written. Affects slash commands, CI scripts, and normal end-of-work wrap-up flows.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm the same root cause across three entry points (post-task, session-end, session save). signals.review_reason: Two reports cover the same || coercion anti-pattern across memory_search and auxiliary commands. The threshold:0 bug breaks an intentional API call ('show me everything'). The 6-sibling audit shows systemic exposure. Non-blocking but affects functional correctness of core memory operations and blocks round-trip data flows.

source_issues.title: Bug: memory_search with threshold: 0 returns empty results due to || coercion (sibling to #1489)

signals.topic: RvfBackend multi-writer silently loses 50-87% of concurrent writes — no error signal to callers
signals.summary: When multiple RvfBackend instances write to the same .rvf file concurrently (multi-process CLI or multi-instance in-process), 50-87% of writes are silently dropped. The snapshot-overwrite race in persistToDiskInner causes last writer to overwrite all others, and lock retry starvation starves writers under N>=8 contention. Zero errors, zero crashes — users get no signal that data was lost.
signals.review_reason: Critical silent data loss with deterministic 100% repro at any N>=2 concurrent writer count. Affects core memory storage path used by hooks, swarm, and multi-pane sessions. Zero error feedback means users cannot detect the loss without external validation. Classified P0 because count=1 but user impact is extreme: production data silently discarded with no signal, every concurrent multi-process or multi-instance invocation is affected.

source_issues.title: RvfBackend: multi-writer silently loses data (snapshot-overwrite race + lock starvation) — fix included
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic 100% repro: N=2 → 50% loss, N=4 → 75% loss, N=8 → 87.5% loss + lock crashes. 20 trials per scenario. No errors, no crash signals to callers. Downstream acceptance suite silently passed because it looked for SQLITE_BUSY (wrong error shape for RVF).

signals.topic: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() missing vectorBackend config — 8 controllers cascade to failed state

ControllerRegistry reports Activated:15 Failed:8 instead of Activated:23 Failed:0.
signals.review_reason: 8 controllers silently fail due to a single missing config field. While only one issue report, the cascade is well-evidenced (controller count before/after), the root cause is confirmed in source, and the fix is non-trivial (naive approach causes regression). Major workflow functionality is disabled without visible error until a user checks controller status.

source_issues.title: Bug: ControllerRegistry.initAgentDB() does not pass vectorBackend config — AgentDB falls back to HNSWLib and vectorBackend controller always returns null
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed in source: controller-registry.ts ~line 498 only passes {dbPath}. Cascades 8 controllers to failed state. A naive hardcoded fix causes regression (dropped from Activated:15 to Activated:4). Requires graceful fallback logic.

The silent success output is deceptive — users believe they are building intelligence when nothing is happening. One report but with extremely detailed evidence and MD5-verified proof of no-op behavior.

signals.topic: CDP reconnection fails silently after external browser restart

Silent failure — no error until user realizes all subsequent operations are dead.

signals.topic: Snapshot serializer strips whitespace around HTML comments, creating false positives on React/Next.js pages

signals.topic: agent-browser open hangs indefinitely on Windows Git Bash, blocking verification workflows

signals.topic: Chrome orphan process persists after network blip, degrading user's normal Chrome profile throughput 17x on macOS
signals.summary: On macOS when a network blip occurs during an active agent-browser session (especially with --profile or --session-name), the spawned Chrome process becomes orphaned, persists indefinitely holding port 9222 and a temp profile directory. This degrades the user's normal Chrome profile throughput from ~700 Mbps to ~36 Mbps until the orphan is manually killed.

source_issues.title: Chrome orphan after network blip during --profile / cookie-bypass sessions on macOS (v0.26.0, regression counterpart to #1157)

Root cause: #1157 fix removed the only process lifecycle guard for Chrome children on macOS. Measurable throughput degradation (17x) with documented numbers.

signals.topic: Tool call approval denial causes streamText to crash with 'Missing required parameter: input[N].output'

The SDK emits tool-output-denied then throws a fatal error, completely breaking the multi-step tool flow with approval.
signals.review_reason: Main flow is completely blocked. Tool approval workflow is a critical feature and denying a tool call should not crash the SDK. Clear reproduction with curl commands and root cause investigation provided. The crash is deterministic and prevents any multi-step flow involving approval denials.

signals.topic: toUIMessageStream({ sendReasoning: false }) leaks reasoning-start/reasoning-end metadata to clients

signals.topic: embed/embedMany crashes at runtime when used with EmbeddingModelV2 providers (warnings undefined)

source_issues.title: embed/embedMany crash: 'warnings' is undefined from EmbeddingModelV2 providers

signals.topic: typedRoutes tsc validation fails to catch invalid Link hrefs in monorepo/workspace setups (link.d.ts not auto-included)
signals.summary: In monorepo or npm workspace setups, next build generates link.d.ts but TypeScript does not automatically include it. As a result, tsc --noEmit cannot catch invalid Link hrefs at build time, defeating the purpose of typedRoutes. Users must manually add a triple-slash reference to .next/types/link.d.ts.
aliases: tsc invalid Link hrefs not enforced workspace
signals.review_reason: typedRoutes is a key type-safety feature of Next.js. When it silently fails in workspace setups, users lose build-time href validation entirely, making runtime 404 errors from broken links likely. The workaround (manual triple-slash reference) is non-obvious and fragile.

signals.topic: Yarn 4 catalog protocol causes turbo query affectedPackages to report false-positive LockfileChanged on unchanged workspaces
